content: Bitwig Controller Extensions (.bwextension) run as Java classes in the Bitwig JVM and are NOT sandboxed against networking. PROVEN (HIGH, cross-referenced primary sources): the DrivenByMoss project ships an Open Sound Control (OSC) extension that sends/receives OSC over UDP, maintained continuously from Bitwig 2.3 (2018) through Bitwig 5.3+ (June 2026) — listed on both the official mossgrabers.de distribution page and the git-moss/DrivenByMoss GitHub repo description. OSC requires opening UDP datagram sockets (java.net.DatagramSocket), proving the extension runtime permits standard java.net networking. INFERRED (MEDIUM, needs spike): because UDP works and extensions use the standard JVM, full java.net (ServerSocket/TCP socket) and ProcessBuilder (child-process/stdio relay) are almost certainly available too, but the OSC success does not by itself prove TCP or process-spawning. The official Bitwig Control Surface API reference ships in-app under Help > Documentation > Developer Resources (confirmed by bitwig/bitwig-extensions README); the repo doc-source folder holds only controller-specific docs, not the API spec.
